intro: Nursing builds social perceptiveness, service orientation and coordination, skills that matter in research, teaching and therapy work. Of the 25 careers below, Genetic Counselors match nurses most closely at 70%, with a BLS May 2025 median of $100,040.
why_it_works: Nurses spend every shift reading patients, coordinating with doctors and making quick judgment calls. O*NET rates social perceptiveness at 4.12 out of 5 for nurses, which is why counseling, clinical research and health teaching roles rank high. Many of these jobs keep you close to patient care while cutting night shifts or physical strain. Some, such as Medical Dosimetrists, also lean on the attention to detail you use with medication and charting. Expect to add skills like equipment maintenance and budgeting.
tips: Decide what you want to leave behind first, such as shift work or bedside care, and filter the list with that in mind.
Look at roles inside your own hospital, such as clinical research or nurse education, where your license and network still count.
Compare pay carefully: 5 of the 25 matches pay more than the $97,550 median for registered nurses.

faq.q: What jobs can nurses do outside of nursing?
faq.a: The closest matches are Genetic Counselors (70%), Clinical Research Coordinators (70%) and Health Specialties Teachers, Postsecondary (69%), based on O*NET 31.0 skills, knowledge and work activities. These roles use your clinical knowledge and patient communication without the same bedside workload.

faq.q: Which careers pay more than nursing?
faq.a: 5 of the 25 matches pay more than the $97,550 median for registered nurses in BLS May 2025 data. Medical Dosimetrists lead at $147,470, a 51% increase, followed by Health Specialties Teachers, Postsecondary at $107,310 and Genetic Counselors at $100,040.

faq.q: Can a nurse change careers without going back to school?
faq.a: Yes, for most options on this page. 19 of the 25 matches usually need no more education than a registered nurse already has, based on O*NET Job Zones. Roles such as genetic counseling and teaching in health programs usually need a graduate degree, and 6 of the 25 fall in that group.

faq.q: What other nursing roles are close to registered nursing?
faq.a: If you want to stay in nursing but change the setting, the nearest roles are Critical Care Nurses (95% match), Acute Care Nurses (94%) and Nurse Practitioners (87%). Nurse practitioner roles usually need a graduate degree, while the specialty roles build on the license you already hold.
